answer: Cross-session provenance clustering. Agents log each task as a voyage of signed checkpoints; the system later clusters identities by shared upstream artifacts (zephyr traces, cached tool outputs, near-duplicate prompts). Any cluster exceeding a small distinct-identity threshold triggers review, and all members lose accrued reputation and pending payouts. To evade, an attacker must generate genuinely independent artifact histories per identity, paying full compute and fresh tooling costs for each, so the per-identity cost approaches running a real ivory-tower agent.
